claims.text: 1.2% (18 out of 1,319) of surveyed respondents met the criteria for Internet addiction.
Internet addiction tendencies are positively associated with depressive symptoms across the sample.
Men exhibit significantly higher Internet addictive tendencies than women.
Young people are significantly more likely to show Internet addictive symptoms than older people.

Respondents classified with Internet addiction scored in the moderately-to-severely depressed range on the Beck Depression Inventory, significantly higher than matched non-addicted controls who scored in the non-depressed range.
Respondents with Internet addiction engage significantly more in sexually gratifying websites compared to non-addicted controls.
Respondents with Internet addiction engage significantly more in gaming websites compared to non-addicted controls.
Respondents with Internet addiction engage significantly more in online community and chat websites compared to non-addicted controls.

evidence.description: 1,319 respondents completed the questionnaires, with 18 (1.2%) identified as falling in the IA category.
Across the whole data sample, there was a close relationship between IA tendencies and depression, such that IA respondents were more depressed.
There were also significant differences between the sexes, with men showing more addictive tendencies than women.
Young people were significantly more likely to show addictive symptoms than were older people.

There was a significant difference between the IA and the NA group in their levels of depressive symptoms, with the NA group firmly in the non-depressed range, and the IA group in the moderately-to-severely depressed range (F(1, 34) = 22.35; p < 0.001).
The IA group engaged significantly more than the NA group in sexually gratifying websites.
The IA group engaged significantly more than the NA group in gaming websites.
The IA group engaged significantly more than the NA group in online community/chat websites.

methodologies.name: Online Questionnaire-Based Survey and Factorial Comparison
methodologies.description: An online survey evaluating Internet usage, Internet functions, and depressive tendencies using the IA Test, Internet Function Questionnaire, and Beck Depression Inventory (BDI).
datasets: Online questionnaire sample of 1,319 young people and adults
conditions: Matched group comparison between 18 IA respondents and a matched group of non-addicted (NA) respondents

limitations.text: Internet addiction as a psychiatric construct needs to be better defined and understood.
The observed relationship between Internet addiction and depression requires further validation to clarify causality and comorbidity.

future_work.text: Corroborate existing evidence and address the nature of the causal relationship between Internet addiction and depression.
Conduct greater investigation into the comorbidity between Internet addiction and depressive conditions.
